# Telegram API pricing in 2026: what is free and what you pay for

Telegram does not charge for its APIs. Costs appear around them: sending above the free limits, digital goods sold for Stars, verification codes, Business accounts and the server your bot runs on.

Published November 4, 2026 Updated November 11, 2026 7 min read

Telegram has no price list for its APIs. You do not pay for creating a bot, for requests or for the number of users. Teams usually start asking about pricing when they plan a large broadcast, sales of digital goods or login codes through Telegram. This article lists what is free, where paid options begin and what a Telegram project costs to run.

## Telegram API pricing at a glance

| What | Price |
|---|---|
| Bot API, Telegram API (MTProto) | Free, no request or user limits on billing |
| Messages within the free limits | Free, about 30 messages per second |
| Paid broadcasts above 30 per second | 0.1 Stars per delivered message |
| Login codes through Telegram Gateway | $0.01 per delivered code |
| Payments for physical goods | No Telegram fee, only the payment provider’s commission |
| Digital goods for Stars | No Telegram fee, developers withdraw $0.013 per Star |
| Bot API server for large files | Free code, you pay for your own hosting |
| Bot replies for a Business account | The account needs Telegram Premium |

## Two APIs, both free

Telegram offers two different APIs, and search results often mix them up.

| API | What it is for | How to get access | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bot API | Bots and Mini Apps: messages, buttons, payments, groups, channels | A token from @BotFather | Free |
| Telegram API (MTProto) | Your own Telegram client or work on behalf of a user account | api_id and api_hash at my.telegram.org | Free |
| TDLib | A ready library for building clients on top of MTProto | Open source, built into your app | Free |

**The Bot API** is what businesses need in almost every case: support bots, shops, booking, Mini Apps. Requests go over HTTPS, and the bot works under its own name with a bot label.

**The Telegram API** works on behalf of a regular account. It is used for alternative clients and for tasks a bot cannot do. Telegram watches how this API is used: mass messaging and spam from user accounts lead to bans, so for communication with customers it is safer to use a bot.

## Free limits of the Bot API

The free tier has limits on speed and file size.

- **About 30 messages per second** to different users and **about one message per second** to a single chat. In groups a bot sends up to 20 messages per minute.
- **A broadcast to 10,000 subscribers** takes around six minutes at these limits. For most businesses this is enough.
- **Files:** a bot downloads files up to 20 MB and uploads up to 50 MB through the standard Bot API.

The file limit is removed with your own Bot API server. Telegram publishes its code for free, and with it a bot uploads files up to 2 GB. You pay only for the hosting.

## Where paid options begin

### Paid broadcasts

Large bots can send up to 1,000 messages per second. Every message above the free 30 per second costs 0.1 Stars from the bot balance, and Telegram charges only for messages that were delivered. The option is turned on in @BotFather and has entry requirements: at least 100,000 Stars on the bot balance and at least 100,000 monthly active users. For a bot with a few thousand users, paid broadcasts are not needed.

### Telegram Stars for digital goods

Digital goods and services inside Telegram are sold for Stars under the platform rules: subscriptions, access to content, paid bot features. Telegram itself takes no commission, but users buy Stars through Apple and Google with their store fees included. Developers withdraw Stars through Fragment at $0.013 per Star, paid in Toncoin. A Star can be withdrawn 21 days after it was received, and the minimum withdrawal is 1,000 Stars. A user who buys 1,000 Stars in the App Store pays about $20, and the developer receives about $13 for them. Plan prices with this gap in mind.

### Payments for physical goods

Physical goods and offline services are paid through a payment provider connected to the bot. Telegram adds no fee of its own, the provider charges its usual commission per payment.

### Verification codes through Gateway

The Telegram Gateway API delivers login and confirmation codes to a user’s Telegram account, as an alternative to SMS. A code costs $0.01, which is usually cheaper than SMS, especially for international numbers. Undelivered codes are refunded automatically, so you pay only for codes that reached the user.

### Telegram Business and Premium

A bot can answer customers on behalf of a business account: it reads and replies to private chats with that account. Connecting a bot this way is a Telegram Business feature, and the account needs a Telegram Premium subscription.

### Ads and usernames

Telegram Ads are paid separately and have nothing to do with the API. A regular username for a bot is free; short collectible usernames are sold at auction on Fragment.

## What a Telegram bot costs to run

The API costs nothing, so the running budget is made of other items:

| Item | When you pay |
|---|---|
| Server | Always: a bot works around the clock |
| Database and backups | When the bot stores orders, users or files |
| Payment provider fee | For every payment for physical goods and services |
| Stars conversion gap | When you sell digital goods |
| Paid broadcasts | Only for very large audiences |
| Gateway codes | If you send login codes through Telegram |
| Premium for Business | If the bot replies on behalf of a business account |
| Support and updates | Monthly, as scenarios and integrations change |

A simple bot runs on an inexpensive virtual server. A Mini App with a database, a catalogue and files needs more resources and a backup plan.

## Free API, paid development

Since the API is free, the main expense is development: scenarios, payments, integrations with your CRM and inventory, an admin panel. What drives that price and how we estimate it is covered in a separate article, [how much a Telegram bot or Mini App costs](https://cloutlab.studio/en/blog/telegram-bot-development-cost/).

## Questions about Telegram API pricing

### Is the Telegram API free?

Yes. The Bot API, the Telegram API (MTProto) and TDLib are free. Telegram does not charge for a bot token, for requests or for the number of users.

### Does the Bot API have a paid plan?

There is no subscription. The only paid part of the Bot API itself is paid broadcasts: 0.1 Stars per message above about 30 messages per second, for bots with at least 100,000 monthly active users.

### How much does Telegram Gateway cost?

$0.01 per delivered verification code. Codes that did not reach the user are refunded.

### Does Telegram take a commission on payments in bots?

No. For physical goods you pay only the payment provider’s commission. For digital goods sold for Stars the cost is the gap between the price users pay in the app stores and the $0.013 per Star that developers withdraw.

### How much does it cost to run a Telegram bot?

The API is free, so the running cost is the server, the database and backups, payment fees and support. A simple bot runs on an inexpensive virtual server.
